claims.text: The presence and degree of chemical short-range order governs oxidation resistance in multiprincipal-element alloys.
SRO directs the preferential nucleation and growth of adherent, multicomponent oxide scales.
Chemical SRO can arise inherently during solidification of MPEAs.
The degree of SRO can be modified through heat treatment.
Rapid solidification or rapid cooling can minimize or otherwise modify SRO.
Nanoscale SRO domains alter local elemental distributions.
SRO alters elemental diffusion pathways at the alloy surface during oxidation.
SRO regions act as barriers to rapid oxygen penetration.
SRO segregates protective-oxide-forming elements and thereby promotes a continuous oxide scale.
Multicomponent oxide scales can form on refractory MPEAs during oxidation between 600 and 900 °C.
The SRO-modified diffusion landscape reduces scale spallation and breakaway oxidation.
Increasing SRO enhances oxidation resistance.
Increasing SRO preserves the mechanical integrity of an alloy during oxidation.
Samples with enhanced SRO will show lower oxidation mass gain over time than samples with minimal SRO.
Samples with enhanced SRO will form more adherent and uniform oxide scales than samples with minimal SRO.
Samples with minimal SRO will undergo greater degradation of mechanical properties during oxidation.
The proposed SRO-controlled oxidation behavior applies to both FCC and BCC MPEAs under isothermal oxidation in air from 600 to 900 °C.
Grain size or defect density can dominate oxidation behavior and cause deviations from the proposed SRO trend.
Distinct heat treatments can produce samples that differ in SRO while retaining otherwise identical overall composition and microstructure.
The quantitative contribution of SRO relative to lattice distortion, dislocation networks, composition, and processing history is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The conditions require processing history to remain constant, but the intervention and comparison explicitly use distinct heat treatments, which are differences in processing history and may alter features other than SRO.
